messages.subject: GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [1]
parts:
Hi,

I wanted to run spde-inla for several larger datasets in a kind of loop, but the function already stops at the beginning in the first step of the loop with this following error message(s):

#######
This application has requested the Runtime to terminate it in an unusual way.
Please contact the application's support team for more information.

This application has requested the Runtime to terminate it in an unusual way.
Please contact the application's support team for more information.


        GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [1]
        Reason    : Alloc failed
        Message   : GSL-library call returned NULL-pointer
        Function  : GMRFLib_density_create
        File      : density.c
        Line      : 1412
        RCSId     : file: density.c  hgid: 4a7cf264b8c8  date: Mon Apr 30 12:42:14 2012 +0200



        GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [1]
        Reason    : Alloc failed
        Message   : Fail to calloc nmemb=zu elements of size=zu bytes
        Function  : GMRFLib_density_create
        File      : density.c
        Line      : 1350
        RCSId     : file: density.c  hgid: 4a7cf264b8c8  date: Mon Apr 30 12:42:14 2012 +0200
#########

Is there anything one could do about this? Or anything you inla guys could fix?
At the moment I am trying to reduce the size of the dataset and see what happens then, but of course it would be great if I can do the analysis with
the full dataset.

Annette

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [1]
parts:
Hi Annette,
It's hard to diagnose the problem from the information you sent. Can
you send some more information.

1) can you run the program with verbose=TRUE and send the full output.
2) what version of R, windows and INLA are you using? (you should
upgrade inla using inla.upgrade(testing=TRUE) )
2a) how much memory your computer has
3) it would also be useful if you could tell us what the likelihood
is, what the latent fields are, the dimension of the latent field(s)
and the number of data points.

Thanks

Dan

Sent from my iPhone
